name: integrate_consensus
content:
# Wave-2 Integration Plan: Consensus Quality + Illusion Detection in the Drainer

## The Integration Point (direct answer)

The integration point is the **drainer's reduction seam**: the boundary where worker outputs are drained out of the flock's outboxes and collapsed into one artifact. Concretely, three hooks bracket the drainer pipeline:

- **Hook A — intake manifests** (before aggregation): nothing enters scoring without provenance.
- **Hook B — the consensus gate** (after scoring, before synthesis/emission): *the* canonical enforcement point. Code-as-law lives here.
- **Hook C — post-synthesis diff audit** (after synthesis, before emit): catches hallucination introduced by the drainer itself.

If you want one sentence for the spec sheet: **Hook B — the deterministic policy gate sitting between consensus scoring (S5) and synthesis (S7), keyed by drain-id, pinned to a signed policy version.**

## Stage Map

```
DrainPipeline:
  S0  intake          enforce WorkerManifest            <- Hook A
  S1  normalize       claim extraction → ClaimAtoms
  S2  CGraph build    entail / contradict / duplicate edges
  S3  CQS scoring     composite score vector
  S4  HID audit       tiered illusion detection
  S5  POLICY GATE     evaluate signed policy → decision <- Hook B
  S6  branch exec     EMIT / STRIP / RECONVENE / QUARANTINE
  S7  diff-audit      emitted-vs-cluster atom delta     <- Hook C
  S8  emit + ledger   append-only commit, prior update
```

## Component Specs as Integrated

### CGraph (consensus graph, S2)
Nodes are claim atoms, not whole messages. Naive string voting gets laundered by paraphrase; we vote on propositions.

- Edge types: `ENTAILS`, `CONTRADICTS`, `DUPLICATES`, weighted by NLI confidence + embedding sim.
- Every node carries provenance: worker_id, trace_id, tool_receipts, span_ref.

### CQS — Consensus Quality Score (S3)
Output is a **vector**, never a bare scalar — the gate rules consume components individually.

- `support_breadth`: mass of agents in the winning cluster.
- `independence_index`: discounts correlated support. Computed from derivation-overlap between supporting rationales (shared n-gram lineage, identical tool-call sequences, trace-lineage intersection). High agreement + low independence = echo chamber, not consensus.
- `contradiction_penalty`: CONTRADICTS edge mass against the winner.
- `margin`: winning cluster mass minus runner-up.
- `calibration_weighted_mass`: each worker vote weighted by its historical Brier-scored reliability prior (fed back from S8).

### HID — Hallucination-Illusion Detector (S4)
Three probes, tiered by cost:

| Tier | Trigger | Check | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | always | dedupe, contradiction edges, citation well-formedness | O(n), static |
| 1 | atoms in winning cluster | grounding probe vs. evidence store / tool receipts → `supported / refuted / unverifiable` | bounded by atom count |
| 2 | CQS in marginal band `[τ_low, τ_high]` OR stakes==high OR echo_suspect | adversarial quorum: spawn k=3 fresh red-team workers with perturbation prompts against contested atoms | expensive, gated |

Illusion classes emitted: `fabricated-entity`, `fabricated-citation`, `unsupported-quantity`, `inherited-hallucination` (corroborated-but-groundless — the swarm-wide shared delusion case), `hedging-erosion` (hedge flipped to assertion). Critical distinction: **agreement is not evidence**. HID exists precisely because the most dangerous failure mode is a confident, unanimous, wrong flock.

## The Gate (Hook B) — Code-as-Law

Decisions come only from evaluating a **signed, versioned policy artifact** against the score vector + HID report. No discretionary overrides at runtime; changing the law is a signed PR to the policy repo. Every gate execution records `policy_version`.

Policy DSL sketch:

```
policy consensus-gate v3:
  rule EMIT_CLEAN:
      cqs.margin >= 0.25
      AND cqs.independence_index >= 0.40
      AND hid.critical_count == 0        # refuted core claims
    -> EMIT

  rule STRIP_MINOR:
      hid.unsupported_count > 0
      AND stakes == LOW
    -> STRIP(stripped_atoms) THEN re-evaluate

  rule RECONVENE_MARGINAL:
      cqs.margin < 0.25
      OR hid.echo_suspect == TRUE
      OR hid.unverifiable_ratio > 0.30
    -> RECONVENE(spec: quorum+20%, tool_forced_grounding=true)

  rule QUARANTINE_REFUTED:
      hid.critical_count > 0
    -> QUARANTINE(reason_codes)

  default -> RECONVENE   # fail closed, never fail open
```

Decision contract:

```
GateDecision {
  drain_id, policy_version,
  action: EMIT | EMIT_FLAGS | STRIP | RECONVENE | QUARANTINE,
  stripped_atom_ids[], reconvene_spec{},
  reason_codes[]
}
```

Note `RECONVENE` handles the contrarian-truth case: a confident correct minority isn't steamrolled by majority — it triggers a re-drain with forced grounding instead of a hard loss.

## Data Contracts (enforced at Hook A)

- `WorkerManifest {worker_id, trace_id, model_rev, tool_receipts[], output_hash}` — payloads without manifests go straight to quarantine. Provenance is non-negotiable because both CQS independence math and HID grounding depend on it.
- `ClaimAtom {id, text, type: fact|inference|spec|citation|quantity, provenance}`
- `EvidenceRef {source, kind: tool|memory|doc|prior, confidence}`
- `ScoreVector`, `HIDReport`, `GateDecision` as above.

## Hook C — Post-Synthesis Diff Audit

Synthesis is itself a generation step and can hallucinate even from clean inputs. Before emit:

1. Atomize the drafted output.
2. Compute set difference vs. union of surviving cluster atoms.
3. Any **novel atom** must either (a) be marked `inference` and be ENTAILED-by-graph, or (b) get stripped.
4. Run hedging-erosion check: hedges present in source atoms that vanished in synthesis flag the artifact.

This closes the loop nobody else watches: **the drainer auditing its own pen**.

## Ledger & Feedback (S8)

Append-only, content-addressed ledger keyed by drain-id:

```
{drain_id, input_hashes, graph_digest, score_vector, hid_report_digest,
 policy_id, decision}
```

Enables full replay of any disputed decision — the operational meaning of code-as-law. Two feedback writes:

- Per-worker outcomes → reliability priors consumed by `calibration_weighted_mass`.
- HID ground-truth confirmations (when later verified) → probe threshold tuning.

## Rollout Sequence

1. **Shadow mode**: gate computes and logs decisions, blocks nothing. Collect real distributions to set `τ_low/τ_high` empirically, not by vibes.
2. Enforce `STRIP`/`QUARANTINE` only; `RECONVENE` still advisory.
3. Full enforcement once strip-precision audits clean on a human-sampled set.
4. Continuous: track reconvene rate, gate override attempts, per-tier latency budget (Tier 2 must remain rare-bandwidth or it becomes the bottleneck).

## Failure-Mode Coverage

| Mode | Caught by |
|---|---|
| Echo-chamber unanimity (agree on a fabrication) | `independence_index` discount + Tier-2 echo probe |
| Paraphrase-laundered disagreement inflating vote counts | CGraph proposition-level voting |
| Confident correct minority | margin rule → RECONVENE, not majority tyranny |
| Synthesis invents beyond sources | Hook C diff + entailment requirement |
| Unprovenanced or spoofed worker output | Hook A manifest quarantine |
| Silent policy tampering | signed policy pinning + ledger replay |

That's the plan. Hooks A/B/C around the reduction seam; the law executes at B.
reasoning:
The user is asking me to act as "Ghost's wave-2 planning engine" — this appears to be a fictional/internal project context. They want me to design how wave-1 designs (quality-of-consensus measurement and hallucination-illusion detection) integrate into a "flock/swarm" architecture, specifically in "the drainer."

Let me parse the terminology:
- "Ghost" — seems to be the name of a system or team
- "wave-2 planning engine" — I'm doing second-wave integration planning
- "code-as-law governance" — governance model where rules are encoded
- "flock/swarm" — multi-agent system (like a swarm of LLM agents)
- "drainer" — some component in the swarm; likely an aggregation/synthesis component that drains outputs from multiple agents into a final result. In swarm terminology, could be the aggregator/reducer.
- "consensus/consensus-illusion designs" from wave-1: quality-of-consensus measurement + hallucination-illusion detection.

So the task: design the concrete integration architecture. Where does consensus quality measurement hook in? Where does illusion detection hook in? The user asks specifically: "Give the integration point." So they want a precise answer about where these plug in — presumably in the drainer's pipeline stages.

Let me think about what a drainer likely is: In a swarm where many worker agents produce candidate answers, the drainer collects (drains) all agent outputs and aggregates them into a final output. It likely runs: normalization → clustering → aggregation/synthesis → verification → emission.

Consensus quality measurement: measures how well agents agree, weighted by reliability, diversity of reasoning paths, etc. Not just majority vote but semantic agreement metrics: embedding similarity clusters, entailment graphs, calibration-weighted confidence, path-diversity checks (do agents agree via independent reasoning chains or copy-paste correlated ones?).

Hallucination-illusion detection: detects when a confident-looking consensus is actually a shared fabrication — e.g., multiple agents trained on same data repeat the same false claim; or the synthesis step introduces unsupported claims; or citation/grounding failures. "Illusion" = consensus that looks like truth but is fabricated. So wave-1 presumably defined detectors for: self-consistency illusions, grounding violations, cross-agent corroboration without evidence (echo chamber), entity/fact verification against tools/memory.

Integration point: the drainer. Specifically:

Design a pipeline inside the drainer with named stages:
1. INTAKE / normalize
2. CLUSTER (semantic agreement graph)
3. CONSENSUS SCORING (CQS — Consensus Quality Score)
4. ILLUSION AUDIT (HID — Hallucination-Illusion Detector)
5. GATE (code-as-law policy enforcement)
6. SYNTHESIS / emit

Key insight: don't run illusion detection only on the final synthesized output; run it at two points: pre-synthesis on the cluster representatives (to catch shared fabrications before they get laundered through aggregation), and post-synthesis on the emitted artifact (to catch synthesis-invented claims). The critical integration point is the gate between scoring and emission — the "consensus gate."

Also code-as-law governance: thresholds encoded as versioned policy artifacts (e.g., policy DSL / signed config), every decision logged with evidence bundle, deterministic evaluation so disputes can be replayed. Governance = machine-checkable rules, not discretionary overrides. So define rule schema: `if CQS < τ_low → reject/quorum re-run; if HID flags ≥ k → strip claims or escalate; etc.`

Let me make it concrete:

**Components:**

- **CGraph** (consensus graph): nodes = normalized claims/propositions extracted from each agent output; edges = entail/contradict/duplicate with weights from NLI + embedding sim. This replaces naive string voting.
- **CQS (Consensus Quality Score)**: composite:
  - support breadth (fraction of agents in agreeing cluster)
  - independence-adjusted support (discount correlated reasoning paths; detect copy-correlation via shared n-grams / trace lineage tags)
  - contradiction penalty (edges contradicting)
  - calibration term (agents' historical reliability priors — Brier-based weights)
  - margin (top cluster mass vs runner-up)
  Output: scalar + vector breakdown.
- **HID (hallucination-illusion detector)**: three probes:
  - grounding probe: every factual atom in winning cluster checked against tool/memory/evidence store → supported/refuted/unverifiable
  - echo probe: corroboration-without-independence detector (same source lineage, near-duplicate derivations, templated phrasing) — catches "swarm-wide shared delusion"
  - stress probe: targeted perturbation prompts to a small adversarial quorum ("red-team slice") sampled per high-stakes claim; cheap because only triggered above stakes threshold.
  Output: per-claim labels + illusion risk score; specific classes: fabricated-entity, fabricated-citation, unsupported-quantitative, inherited-hallucination (from shared training/tool), synthesized-invention (introduced at synthesis).

**Integration points in the drainer** — be very precise since they asked:

Primary integration point: **the drain boundary** — the moment outputs leave workers' outboxes and enter the drainer's reduction pipeline. Concretely three hooks:

1. **Hook A — pre-aggregation (claim extraction & graph build)**: as each worker artifact drains in, extract claim atoms, attach provenance (worker id, trace id, tool receipts). This feeds CGraph. Integration contract: every drained payload must carry a manifest (schema-enforced; payloads without manifests are quarantined).
2. **Hook B — the consensus gate (between scoring and synthesis/emission)**: THE canonical integration point. Code-as-law gate evaluates CQS vector + HID labels against the signed policy. Outcomes: EMIT / EMIT-WITH-FLAGS / STRIP-CLAIMS / RE-CONVENE (spawn re-drain with expanded quorum or tool-forced grounding) / QUARANTINE. Deterministic, replayable.
3. **Hook C — post-synthesis audit**: run HID again over final artifact diffed against winning cluster — catch synthesis-introduced atoms not present in any worker output ("the drainer itself hallucinating"). Diff = new atoms must carry explicit inference markers or get stripped.

Also mention feedback loop: outcomes write back to worker reliability priors (calibration), closing the loop for future CQS weighting. And governance ledger: append-only log keyed by drain-id containing inputs hash, graph digest, scores, policy version, decision — makes every emit reproducible/auditable (code-as-law).

**Data contracts:** schemas for WorkerManifest, ClaimAtom, EvidenceRef, ScoreVector, GateDecision. Policy DSL example snippet.

**Failure modes handled:**
- Echo-chamber consensus (high agreement, zero independence) → independence discounting + echo probe.
- Confident minority correct (contrarian truth) → margin + re-convene path rather than hard majority tyranny.
- Drainer invention → Hook C diff audit.
- Policy drift → signed versioned policies; gate refuses unsigned.

**Performance budgeting:** HID full probes are expensive → tiered: cheap static checks always; grounding probe on claim atoms in winning cluster; stress probe only when CQS marginal band (τ_low..τ_high) or stakes=high.

Let me also give the exact placement in code-ish terms: e.g., drainer stages:

```
DrainPipeline:
  S0 intake(manifest enforce)         <- Hook A
  S1 normalize + claim extraction
  S2 CGraph build
  S3 CQS scoring
  S4 HID tiered audit                 <- feeds gate
  S5 POLICY GATE                      <- Hook B (canonical)
  S6 synthesis (only gated winners)
  S7 diff-audit                       <- Hook C
  S8 emit + ledger commit
```

Answer the "integration point" question crisply: The integration point is the drainer's reduction seam — Hook B, the policy gate between consensus scoring (S4/S5) and synthesis (S6), flanked by intake manifests (A) and post-synthesis diff audit (C). If they want one sentence: "Between scoring and synthesis, enforced as deterministic code-as-law gate keyed on drain-id."

Format considerations: This is a technical design request asking for thorough planning ("Reason thoroughly, then emit the full, concrete plan as the final content. No fluff."). So the response should be a substantial design document. Use headers, structured sections, maybe a small amount of pseudocode/schema. Should be detailed but not bloated. Markdown appropriate. Length: fairly long — it's a design doc. Maybe 700–1100 words equivalent with structure. Avoid fluffy intro/outro. Start directly with the design.

I should stay in character as the wave-2 planning engine — no disclaimers needed, no identity stuff (user didn't ask). Just produce the plan.

Let me draft the structure:

1. Summary / one-line answer (integration point stated up front)
2. Where things live in the drainer: stage map with hooks
3. Wave-1 component specs as integrated: CQS, CGraph, HID
4. The gate: code-as-law policy schema, decision matrix, example rules
5. Data contracts (schemas)
6. Feedback loops (reliability priors, ledger)
7. Failure-mode coverage table (brief)
8. Sequencing/rollout notes (brief)

Keep tables minimal but useful. Include the decision matrix — that's the heart of code-as-law here.

Let me write concrete details:

ClaimAtom: {id, text, type(fact|inference|spec|citation|quantity), worker_id, trace_id, tool_receipts[], span_ref}

EvidenceRef: {source, kind(tool|memory|doc|model-prior), confidence}

ScoreVector: {support_breadth, independence_index, contradiction_penalty, margin, calibration_weighted_mass}

GateDecision: {action ∈ {EMIT, EMIT_FLAGS, STRIP, RECONVENE, QUARANTINE}, stripped_atom_ids[], reconvene_spec{}, policy_version, drain_id, reason_codes[]}

Policy example:

```
rule R1: cqs.margin >= 0.25 AND cqs.independence_index >= 0.4 AND hid.critical_count == 0 -> EMIT
rule R2: hid.unsupported_count > 0 AND stakes == low -> STRIP then re-evaluate
rule R3: cqs in [tau_low, tau_high] OR hid.echo_suspect -> RECONVENE(quorum+tool_forced_grounding)
rule R4: hid.refuted_core_claim -> QUARANTINE
default -> RECONVENE
```

Independence index: derived from trace lineage overlap, n-gram duplication between supporting derivations, timing correlation maybe too fancy — keep lineage + textual derivation overlap.

Echo probe specifics: build derivation-similarity between supporting rationales; if pairwise overlap > θ and no divergent chain among supporters → mark echo_suspect; discount independence.

Tiering:
- Tier 0 (always): dedupe, contradiction edges, citation format check — O(n)
- Tier 1 (winning cluster atoms): grounding probe against evidence store/tools — bounded by atom count
- Tier 2 (marginal band or high stakes): adversarial quorum stress test, k=3 fresh workers with perturbation prompts, majority-of-red-team verdict per contested atom

Post-synthesis diff (Hook C): set difference between emitted artifact atoms and union of winning-cluster atoms → any novel atom must have `inference` marker + be entailed-by-graph check; else strip. Also detect synthesis-level smoothing that flips a hedged claim into unqualified assertion (hedging erosion check).

Ledger: append-only, content-addressed; entry = {drain_id, input_hashes, graph_digest, score_vector, hid_report_digest, policy_id, decision}. Enables dispute replay. Code-as-law means: decisions only from evaluated policy; humans amend law by PR to policy repo, signed; gate pins policy_version per decision.

Rollout: shadow mode first (gate logs would-be decisions, doesn't block), then enforce on STRIP/QUARANTINE actions, then full enforcement; tune taus from shadow distribution.

Metrics to watch: gate override rate, reconvene rate, strip precision (human audit sample), latency budget per tier.

I think that covers it. Now formatting: headers, tight bullets, one small code block for pipeline, one for policy, maybe compact schema list. Keep it dense and concrete. No preamble fluff — maybe one line stating the integration point answer immediately, since that was the direct question.
